It applies to pretraining, supervised training, classifier inference, canonical-null workflows, prototype extraction/scoring and pairwise-comparison. Dataset/factory Python APIs accept the same modes, defaulting to chunking_mode="auto".

Both inferred methods support primary/unmapped DNA/RNA A/C/G/T reads with the appropriate 9-mer current model. They use positive integer ts as the signal start and ns as the exclusive end. A zero or absent ts triggers start estimation; an absent ns triggers end estimation. If both are missing, both endpoints are estimated. Character-valued ts:A alignment tags are ignored. Invalid numeric bounds raise an error. Secondary/supplementary records are excluded. Tags always describe acquisition-time coordinates; RNA signal is reversed after trimming to follow original read sequence order. This does not depend on the alignment strand. Other k-mer model sizes remain supported by mv only.

Both methods use six-sample non-overlapping means and quantile-based affine calibration for matching. The defaults are:

  • hierarchical: 192-base interior anchor queries, approximately 256-base anchor spacing, endpoint queries up to 384 bases, and piecewise interpolation. RNA search, duration and cost bounds scale with estimated signal dwell.
  • dtw: whole-read one-to-many DTW with a sloped half-band of 1,000 averaged bins (6,000 raw samples), squared-current error, rolling cost rows and byte traceback pointers. Known ts/ns endpoints bypass anchor searches. Missing endpoints are estimated by the hierarchy before DTW. The traceback is capped at 256 MiB per read; oversized or unreachable alignments raise an error, without silently switching methods. Hierarchical is available for very long reads that exceed this allocation limit.

The model receives original signal samples at its configured row width. Fewer than one row of terminal samples may be dropped to preserve that width. Inferred boundaries do not supply move tables or measured per-base dwell times.

docs.title: Inference input options
docs.text: Start with input preparation and the supervised guide. This page covers direct options, JSON input, read exclusion, and POD5 indexing.

docs.title: Direct supervised inference inputs
docs.text:
porefm detect-modification accepts sample settings directly, as an alternative to --bam_config. Both routes use the same supervised sample validation and defaults. For example:

porefm detect-modification \
  --model WGLab/PoreFM-RNA_m6A-Inosine@v0.1.0 \
  --bam_path basecalls.bam --pod5 pod5/ \
  --read_based --ref reference.fa --motif 'A 0' \
  --output outputs/supervised

The direct options correspond to fields within a JSON labelled_samples entry:

CLI option JSON field Meaning / default --bam_path bam_path BAM file or recursive SG BAM directory; multiple paths share the same settings. --pod5 pod5 Raw signal file or recursive directory; otherwise use SG tags. Requires one BAM file. --bam_index bam_index Optional saved read-ID index; requires POD5. --ref ref Indexed reference FASTA. Required for reference-based targets. --contigs, --chrom contigs Whitespace-separated contig names; default: all. --read_based read_based Select motifs in basecalls; default: reference-based selection. --motif motif Quoted motif/offset expression, e.g. 'A 0' or 'DRACH 2'. --pos_file pos_file Reference-position table; mutually exclusive with --motif and incompatible with --read_based. --motif_label motif_label Target class index or semicolon-delimited indices; default: 0. Does not restrict predicted classes. --flag flag Additional SAM flag bits to exclude; default: 0. --sample_labels sample_labels Per-chunk-occurrence target retention probability in [0, 1]; default: 1. --polish, --use_polished_sequence polish Enable reference-based sequence polishing; default: disabled. --polish_indel_limit polish_indel_limit Maximum insertion/deletion length to polish; default: 5. --polish_vcf_path polish_vcf_path Variants to preserve during polishing; requires --polish.

These sample options also accept hyphenated spellings, such as --bam-path and --read-based. Paths are used relative to the working directory, just as in JSON. Read-based selection requires --motif; reference-based selection requires --ref and exactly one of --motif or --pos_file.

For read-based inference, a supplied --ref retains available reference coordinates for aligned reads. Motifs still select positions in the called read sequence. This differs from training label selection, where the unscoped read-based motif loader does not use a reference to define labels.

Direct sample settings cannot be combined with --bam_config (also --bam-config), except for its global --read_based override. Use JSON for independently configured samples or tagged label sources. Training-only label smoothing and supervision policies remain JSON/training settings. Model, output, preprocessing, and resource options apply to either input route. Direct runs record the normalized sample config and its defaults under arguments.resolved_input in run_manifest.json.

docs.title: Excluding reads from detection
docs.text:
porefm detect-modification (alias porefm infer) accepts --exclude-bed regions.bed, also spelled --exclude_bed. The same file applies to every configured sample, including SG BAM and POD5 inputs, in reference-based or read-based mode. Omitting the option disables region exclusion.

The file must contain three or four whitespace-separated columns: chrom start end [strand], with zero-based, half-open reference coordinates. Three-column rows match both strands; column four, when present, must be + or - and matches the BAM alignment strand, including for RNA. Blank lines and # comments are allowed; named BED4 or BED6 files must first be converted to this format.

Any overlap with a read's full reference span excludes the entire read before signal decoding and model scoring, including overlaps inside deletions or introns. Touching an interval endpoint is not an overlap. Unmapped reads are not excluded by this option and remain subject to the other input filters. The file is validated before checkpoint loading or output creation, and the startup manifest records its path and SHA-256 digest. Region exclusion uses ncls, which is included in the standard PoreFM installation.

docs.title: POD5 signal input for inference
docs.text:
porefm detect-modification accepts --pod5 with direct --bam_path input, or pod5 on one JSON labelled_samples entry. A POD5 run must contain exactly one sample and one BAM file: BAM directories, multiple BAMs and mixed SG/POD5 samples are rejected. Supply one .pod5 file or a directory; directories are searched recursively for *.pod5 files.

Build an optional reusable index before inference:

porefm utils index-bam --bam /path/to/basecalls.bam --threads 4

This creates /path/to/basecalls.bam.pfmi beside the BAM. The .pfmi suffix is appended to the full filename. Use --output /other/path/custom.pfmi to choose a different index destination.

index-bam includes every BAM record, including secondary, supplementary, unmapped, low-quality and no-move-table records. It applies no inference filters. It saves a SQLite lookup of parent/read IDs to BAM virtual offsets, without signals or sequences. It needs no BAI and does not modify the BAM. The output must be a new path; existing files are never overwritten. An output pointing to the BAM itself, including via symbolic or hard links, is rejected. An adjacent <bam_path>.pfmi is discovered automatically. To supply an index explicitly, use --bam_index with direct inputs, or bam_index in the same JSON sample entry:

{
  "config_type": "supervised",
  "schema_version": 1,
  "labelled_samples": [
    {
      "bam_path": "/path/to/basecalls.bam",
      "pod5": "/path/to/pod5_directory",
      "bam_index": "/path/to/basecalls.bam.pfmi",
      "read_based": true,
      "motif": "A 0",
      "motif_label": 0
    }
  ]
}

The BAM supplies sequence, move tables and alignments; POD5 supplies raw int16 ADC signal. When pod5 is present it takes precedence over any SG tag. Omit pod5 to read signal from SG tags. Reference-based motif/position samples can also use pod5 with their reference and target fields.

The same index can be reused with different quality, length, motif, region and POD5-subset settings. Inference checks that the index still matches the BAM. Rebuild after rewriting or recompressing the BAM, and do not modify it during indexing or inference. bam_index requires pod5. Explicit indexes take precedence over automatic discovery and must exist and validate.

Without bam_index, inference first checks for <bam_path>.pfmi alongside the BAM. If absent, it reuses or builds an unfiltered, reusable index at OUTPUT_DIR/BAM_FILENAME.pfmi before starting DataLoader workers. For example, /data/reads.bam falls back to OUTPUT_DIR/reads.bam.pfmi. Automatic builds write to the output directory. They leave the input BAM path and contents unchanged. Distributed inference builds the index once and shares it across workers. A valid automatically discovered index is reused; an invalid or stale index raises an error. Output-directory safety rules apply, including --force-overwrite when intentionally reusing a run directory. The generated index can also be supplied explicitly to a later run. Unmatched POD5 reads are skipped without decoding signal. BAM sorting and a BAI/CSI index are unnecessary for this path, including when contigs filters the records. Secondary and supplementary alignments are excluded. Move tables are preferred; in the default auto chunking mode, supported chemistries can infer chunks for reads without moves. Explicit mv mode skips those reads. Ordinary reads match by query name. Dorado child reads match their pi parent ID, and their sp sample offsets are applied before the usual ts/mv trimming and RNA orientation. Each parent's signal is decoded once for all its eligible children. POD5 subsets emit only matching BAM records. Files processed by different workers must contain disjoint read IDs. Repeated IDs within one worker are suppressed; aliases of the same path are removed during discovery.

POD5 inputs produce unordered results, and BAM output is marked SO:unsorted. Training continues to require SG signal BAMs. The JSON option applies to porefm detect-modification labelled samples, not tagged training sample definitions.

Zero-shot detection (porefm zero-shot detect) and porefm prototype classify (including --scorer residual-effects) accept the equivalent CLI options alongside their scoring arguments:

--bam_path /path/to/basecalls.bam \
--pod5 /path/to/pod5_directory \
--bam_index /path/to/basecalls.bam.pfmi \
--output_dir /path/to/new_run

For these commands, omitting --bam_index uses the same adjacent-index discovery and output-directory fallback before model loading and DataLoader startup. --bam_index requires --pod5. The single-BAM-file contract, child-read slicing, region/quality filters and POD5-file worker assignment are shared with supervised inference. Zero-shot detection and prototype scoring use one process/GPU with multiple DataLoader workers. Prototype extraction and canonical-null training/calibration require SG signal BAMs.

POD5 files are assigned disjointly to ranks and then DataLoader workers. The requested --dataloader_workers (--num_workers in the scoring commands) is capped to the number of files assigned to that rank: one POD5 file uses at most one worker; zero workers processes input in the main process. SG input assigns whole BAM files to workers. POD5 signal goes directly to preprocessing without an intermediate SG conversion.

docs.title: Advanced output analysis
docs.text: Start with the output guide for a preview and a site summary. This page covers SQL, specialized pairwise diagnostics, and selecting labels for downstream analyses. All examples read completed output files.

docs.title: DuckDB
docs.text:
This example uses a completed prototype run. Adjust its path and class labels to your model:

from porefm.outputs import open_output
calls = open_output("outputs/prototype")

import duckdb

with duckdb.connect() as con:
    con.execute("SET memory_limit='8GB'")
    calls.register(con, name="calls", filters={"call_status": "called"})
    df = con.sql("""
        SELECT chrom, position, predicted_class
        FROM calls
        WHERE readname = 'read-id-1'
    """).df()

These are reusable Parquet views. A split-file query can do substantial join work even with LIMIT; use iter_tables for a quick sequential preview. SQL leaves packed contexts as bytes. View rows have no guaranteed order; use ORDER BY if needed.

docs.title: Pairwise diagnostics
docs.text:
Specialized pairwise diagnostics are available from porefm.outputs:

from porefm.outputs import (
    load_pairwise_directory, summarize_pairwise_loci, add_reference_base,
    iter_pairwise_locus_summaries,
)

# Medium comparison runs use the refname/p_value column names.
pairwise_output_dir = "outputs/pairwise"
reads, site_metrics = load_pairwise_directory(pairwise_output_dir)
loci, annotated_reads = summarize_pairwise_loci(reads, site_metrics)

# Large runs: preserve exact quantiles, PCA fits and cross-fit diagnostics
# while holding only one complete partition at a time.
for stem, loci, _ in iter_pairwise_locus_summaries(
    pairwise_output_dir, return_annotated=False,
):
    consume(loci)

loci = add_reference_base(loci, reference_fasta)

These specialized functions use refname and p_value column names. Grouped results exclude negative reference positions. Advanced fits need the whole current partition in RAM; they cannot be combined from arbitrary partial-locus batches. Loci repeated across partitions raise an error. They preserve control PCA covariance checks and read/locus duplicate detection. The simpler shared SQL summary does not compute exact quantiles or refit PCA.

Site tables written by the comparison can be read without scanning read rows:

comparison = open_output(pairwise_output_dir)
site_metrics = comparison.read_site_table(kind="anomaly_site_metrics")
# comparison.iter_site_tables(...) provides bounded batches instead.

These select only companions of the snapshot's read parts. They contain original producer coverage/covariance, not values recomputed after read filters. add_reference_base accepts chrom or refname, complements bases on reverse-strand sites, and retains zero-based genomic coordinates.

docs.title: Select read-position labels with bounded intermediates
docs.text:
select_quantile_labels and select_threshold_labels accept an existing open_output snapshot and return sorted, deduplicated readname, read_pos, label triples. Both reconstruct one source part at a time. They apply class, status, and optional chromosome filters before selection, exclude nonfinite scores, and use strict comparisons: positive scores above the cutoff and negative scores below it. Class names, score columns, and output label IDs are configurable; positive and negative class sets must be disjoint. The example below assumes a DNA prototype run with C, 5mC, and 5hmC classes; adapt the labels and score column for other models.

from porefm.outputs import select_quantile_labels, select_threshold_labels

common = dict(
    score_column="score_5mC",
    positive_classes=["5mC", "5hmC"], negative_classes=["C"],
    chroms=None, positive_label=1, negative_label=0,
    threads=4, memory_limit="16GB",
    temp_directory="/path/to/node-local-scratch", progress=True,
)

final_df = select_quantile_labels(
    calls, **common, positive_quantile=.75, negative_quantile=.05,
    quantile_partitions=32,
)

# An output path avoids constructing the final pandas DataFrame as well.
label_path = select_threshold_labels(
    calls, **common, positive_threshold=300, negative_threshold=-300,
    negative_ratio=1.0, random_state=42,
    output_path="labels.parquet",
)

The quantile helper's first pass writes only group/cohort/score to temporary Parquet, partitioned by a hash of (group, cohort). Each partition pools all source parts and computes exact interpolated quantiles. The second source pass applies those thresholds and writes only selected labels. This preserves global per-k-mer quantiles, including duplicate contributions before selection; it does not average per-part quantiles or use approximate quantiles. group_column defaults to kmer. More quantile_partitions reduce simultaneous aggregate state at the cost of additional files; an exceptionally large individual group still needs memory for its exact quantile state.

The fixed-threshold helper never projects k-mers or sequences. It writes eligible label triples per part, then samples floor(negative_ratio * n_positive) negative rows without replacement before deduplication. negative_ratio=None retains all negatives; insufficient negatives raise. An integer seed makes the negative-row sampling reproducible for fixed inputs. The permutation requires 8 bytes of temporary disk per eligible negative on a 64-bit system; mapped pages are managed by the OS.

Each invocation owns a unique work directory under temp_directory, including its DuckDB spill directory, and cleans it on normal completion or exceptions. When omitted, the parent is the system temporary directory rather than .tmp under the working directory. Choose disk-backed node-local scratch with enough space; NFS spill directories can fail with stale file handles. Abrupt process termination can leave temporary files behind.

The final global sort/deduplication can spill to disk. Returning pandas still requires RAM for the final result; memory_limit is not a hard process-RAM cap. With output_path, sorted Parquet is published atomically and its absolute Path is returned. The destination must not exist and must be outside input-part directories. Input files must remain unchanged during a call, especially the quantile helper's two passes; newly published parts are excluded from the fixed snapshot.

docs.title: Signal dropout during training
docs.text: These options apply when training models. Running a released inference model does not require changing its checkpoint configuration. For input JSON, see configuration formats.

docs.title: Signal-modality dropout during pretraining
docs.text:
Signal-modality dropout trains the model with one signal representation occasionally withheld. During pretraining, --signal_dropout_prob P independently chooses one action for each batch item: drop percentile features with probability P/2, drop raw-signal features with probability P/2, or keep both with probability 1-P. The choice is broadcast across that batch item. Inference and supervised classification use zero signal dropout.

Choose how the EMA target encoder handles dropout with --ema_signal_dropout_mode:

  • independent: sample separate batch-item choices for the student and EMA target;
  • shared: reuse each student's choice for the corresponding EMA batch item;
  • disabled (default): apply configured dropout to the student while keeping EMA target modality dropout off.

Checkpoints save both settings. --use_loaded_config and --resume inherit them when the corresponding CLI options are omitted. Resume requires the saved settings; a warm start without --resume may override them. Evaluation uses zero signal dropout.

docs.title: Auxiliary pretraining during fine-tuning
docs.text: With --train_pretrain_tasks, auxiliary batches may use an explicit value with --pretrain_signal_dropout_prob, or use the checkpoint value with --use_loaded_pretrain_signal_dropout_prob. The EMA mode inherits from the checkpoint unless --pretrain_ema_signal_dropout_mode overrides it. These options are rejected when auxiliary pretraining is disabled.

docs.title: Fit a custom effect model
docs.text: Released prototype bundles are ready for inference. Use this reference when fitting effects from your own matched modified and canonical data. Read the scoring model before selecting a recipe.

docs.title: Fit inputs
docs.text:
Create a JSON manifest using the fields below. Relative paths are resolved against the manifest directory. The neighborhood files must be extracted first. Paths in the command examples are placeholders for your own data, checkpoints, and manifests.

Each canonical family has:

  • label: output class name; U is encoded as T internally.
  • prototypes: nonempty list of canonical context tables, all with the same odd k. Repeated contexts are pooled by observation count.
  • noise_prototypes: optional list of canonical reservoirs, defaulting to prototypes. Noise contexts may use a different k from the baseline.

All four canonical families are required, including families without a modeled modification, because they receive other bases' footprints. Each modifications entry has label, canonical, prototype, control_prototype, and footprint_pairs. Each pair supplies modified and control neighborhood files plus a single-base BED6, with 0-based half-open coordinates and explicit strand. BED name/score fields are not interpreted as class labels. The caller must supply every known event of that type, not just evaluation target sites. Control samples must actually be unmodified; filenames cannot prove this.

To use IVT 9-mer data, put canonical-only 9-mer reservoirs from prototype extract-kmer-prototypes --kmer_size 9 --reservoir_size ... in each family's prototypes and noise_prototypes. A shared all-base reservoir may be listed once per family; the fitter selects that family's center base. Keep each modification's matched 5-mer oligo control in control_prototype. Do not subtract unrelated IVT means to estimate the modification effect. This implements the 9-mer canonical baseline plus 5-mer transferable-effect model; it does not infer modification-specific outer-flank interactions absent from the labeled data.

Relevant manifest defaults:

Setting Default Meaning kmer_size 5 Effect context length footprint_radius 4 Read-oriented footprint support; 0 fits center-only canonical_mean_mode shrunken empirical, regression, or count-shrunken blend canonical_unseen regression Fallback for unseen empirical/shrunken contexts; alternatively no-call canonical_ridge 10 Canonical sequence-regression ridge effect_mode regression empirical, regression, or mixed effect_ridge 10 Center-effect regression ridge effect_shrinkage 0.5 Global-center shrinkage α, as defined below; 0 disables it effect_mix_weight 0.5 Empirical weight u in mixed mode; not estimated from read counts effect_unseen no-call Empirical-only missing-context policy; alternatively global footprint_ridge 10 Independent off-center footprint ridge footprint_shrinkage 0.5 Independent footprint shrinkage toward offset/receiving-base effects canonical_strength 32 Pseudocount favoring the canonical sequence regression noise_mode base base, hierarchical-5mer, or none (identity metric) noise_shrinkage 0.1 Isotropic covariance shrinkage noise_floor 1e-6 Absolute covariance diagonal floor noise_local_strength 512 Pseudodegrees of freedom for local-to-base covariance pooling noise_local_shrinkage null Optional fixed local-to-base weight in [0,1], replacing the count heuristic noise_samples_per_context 256 Deterministic uniform subsample cap per source/context min_count 2 Minimum canonical/paired mean support modification_penalty 4 Per-event cost in whitened Gaussian score units seed 0 Noise subsampling seed

These defaults are starting values, not empirically calibrated thresholds. Reservoir contribution is observation-weighted up to the cap, not uniformly weighted over all contexts or samples. Avoid duplicated input reads/tables.

docs.title: Choose fitting settings
docs.text: These are fit-time controls, available as manifest keys and identically named prototype fit-effect-prototypes CLI flags. CLI values override manifest globals. Each modification entry may additionally override effect_mode, effect_shrinkage, effect_mix_weight, effect_unseen, and effect_ridge; these more-specific settings take precedence over globals. All resolved values are stored in the artifact and reported during fitting.

docs.title: Canonical mean
docs.text:
• --canonical_mean_mode empirical: observed means without shrinkage. On observed contexts this equals setting canonical_strength=0 in the default recipe. By default an unseen context still uses regression; add --canonical_unseen no-call to disable that fallback and skip canonical regression training entirely.
  • --canonical_mean_mode regression: use the regression for every context.
  • --canonical_mean_mode shrunken: a count-weighted blend of empirical and regression estimates.

docs.title: Center modification effect
docs.text:
Let d be the matched empirical modified−control difference for one 5-mer, dhat the unshrunk ridge prediction for that 5-mer, and dbar the global average of empirical differences across paired 5-mers. α is effect_shrinkage; u is effect_mix_weight. They are scalar weights, not learned predictors. The three recipes are:

effect_mode Effect used on an observed paired 5-mer empirical (1−α) d + α dbar regression (1−α) dhat + α dbar mixed u d + (1−u) [(1−α) dhat + α dbar]

Thus empirical does not force a choice between raw and shrunken effects: α=0 gives raw d, and α>0 shrinks d toward dbar. Mixed mode does not shrink its empirical branch a second time. Its weights on d, dhat, and dbar are u, (1−u)(1−α), and (1−u)α, respectively.

On unseen 5-mers, regression and mixed use the regression/global estimate (mixed sets u=0). Empirical mode defaults to a no-call, or uses dbar when --effect_unseen global is specified. If any compatible class lacks a required empirical effect, the position is a no-call, not a forced canonical call. A missing empirical hypothesis also masks observations in its possible footprint, so overlapping candidate footprints are conservatively unscorable (up to 2R away). This prevents an unsupported neighbor from being silently treated as canonical; compare recipes on shared callable positions. A footprint training event with an unsupported center effect raises an error; provide paired support or explicitly select a fallback.

For initial comparisons, use regression, raw empirical, and optionally empirical with α=0.5. Add mixed mode if neither suffices; start with fixed u=0.5. Large read counts from one construct do not establish that its effects transfer reliably to other sequence contexts.

Center-effect changes also change what is subtracted during footprint fitting, so refit the artifact when changing these modes. The independent footprint_ridge and footprint_shrinkage controls prevent a center-effect ablation from silently changing footprint regularization. Empirical center mode disables center regression, not the separate off-center footprint fit. Likewise canonical_ridge is separate from effect_ridge.

docs.title: Canonical noise
docs.text:
--noise_mode none uses identity whitening and does not require saved noise reservoirs. base uses one metric per canonical base. hierarchical-5mer requires kmer_size=9 canonical noise reservoirs; 5-mer input is rejected.

For each source/9-mer group, subtract its own sampled mean first. Pool the resulting scatter and degrees of freedom by central 5-mer. Let S_c denote that 5-mer's empirical covariance, C_b the already regularized base-level covariance, ε the configured noise floor, and I the identity matrix. The local covariance is:

C_c = (1−η_c) (S_c + ε I) + η_c C_b

By default η_c = noise_local_strength / (noise_local_strength + df_c); df_c is the sum of (sampled_count−1) over contributing source/9-mer groups. Alternatively, --noise_local_shrinkage VALUE fixes η for all supported 5-mers. η=0 gives local covariance plus floor, and η=1 exactly reproduces the pooled base metric. This is a configurable shrinkage heuristic, not an estimated Ledoit-Wolf optimum. Isotropic noise_shrinkage applies to the base target.

An unseen complete receiving 5-mer falls back to C_b; an incomplete 5-mer is unavailable. The same receiving-position matrix whitens observations, center effects, and all incoming footprints. No covariance is estimated from queries. Prefer a 9-mer canonical baseline alongside this noise model, so unmodeled outer-flank mean shifts are not mistaken for modifications. The covariance could have good support even if individual 9-mers are sparse, because many 9-mers share the same central 5-mer.

All 1,024 float32 512×512 local whitening matrices occupy about 1 GiB. Scoring uses shared matrix views, not an expanded read-length×512×512 array. Fitting also needs temporary scatter storage; only one base family is fitted at a time. Inspect the saved local counts/degrees/pooling weights when judging support. Centering before pooling prevents 9-mer mean differences from being counted as canonical noise.

docs.title: Example fit overrides
docs.text:
Keep all source paths in a manifest, then change only these flags between fits:

# No canonical shrinkage; raw empirical modification effects.
porefm prototype fit-effect-prototypes \
  --manifest /path/to/effect-manifest.json \
  --canonical_mean_mode empirical --effect_mode empirical --effect_shrinkage 0 \
  --output outputs/prototype_effects/empirical.pt

# Requires a manifest whose noise_prototypes point to genuine IVT 9-mer files.
porefm prototype fit-effect-prototypes \
  --manifest /path/to/ivt9-manifest.json \
  --effect_mode mixed --effect_mix_weight 0.5 --effect_shrinkage 0.5 \
  --noise_mode hierarchical-5mer --noise_local_strength 512 \
  --output outputs/prototype_effects/mixed_hierarchical.pt

The fitted artifact records the resolved settings, empirical support, and local noise tables.

docs.title: Extract neighborhoods and fit
docs.text:
Fitting and scoring saved embeddings use CPU. Fresh backbone extraction supports CPU but a GPU is preferable for volume. The following extracts the four neighborhood files used in the example. It can be limited with --max_batches for a small trial run. Full references are restricted to 10 Mb and statistics to --max_sites.

data=/path/to/oligo-data
backbone=/path/to/backbone-checkpoint

for sample in control_A m6A control_C m5C; do
  case "$sample" in control_A|m6A) base=A ;; control_C|m5C) base=C ;; esac
  porefm prototype extract-effect-neighborhoods \
    --bam_path "$data/signal_bams/$sample.signal.bam" \
    --ref "$data/references/${base}_reference.fasta" \
    --model_path "$backbone" \
    --size 2048 --step 1800 --num_trim 8 \
    --min_qscore 10 --min_base_quality 10 --kmer_size 5 --radius 4 \
    --embedding_key contextual_base_seq --device cuda --disable_compile \
    --output "outputs/prototype_effects/neighborhoods/$sample.pt"
done

porefm prototype fit-effect-prototypes \
  --manifest /path/to/effect-manifest.json \
  --output outputs/prototype_effects/model.pt --threads 4

Neighborhood extraction retains only exact contiguous k-mers whose bases pass the quality threshold, with one reference-position observation per read. Both strands use genomic coordinates while sequences and effect offsets follow read orientation. Matched statistics must record identical QC settings. It uses the production signal normalization/chunking path, not cached basecalls alone.

docs.title: Prototype output files and BAM tags
docs.text: For everyday analysis, start with processing outputs. This reference describes stored fields, completion checks, and optional BAM tags.

docs.title: Output and safeguards
docs.text:
All input chunks participate in inference, even if --pos_file or --motif requests output for only one base family. Chunks are stitched by greatest edge margin before classification; selection labels never identify the true neighbors. In aligned mode, inserted and soft-clipped bases can supply observed embeddings and read-derived contexts even though they have no reference coordinate. Only reported rows require an aligned reference position; an insertion alone does not invalidate neighboring calls. Neighborhood-statistics extraction still applies its exact read/reference-match and base-quality filters. effect_run.json records observation_validity=observed_read_tokens_independent_of_reference_alignment.

A candidate needs complete source/canonical sequence contexts and valid observations throughout its footprint. Missing contexts give class index -1, null scores, and call_status=unavailable_context, not a canonical call. This includes missing empirical support when its configured policy is no-call. Consequently the center-only ablation has more callable edge positions; compare methods on their shared callable positions.

By default, inference writes paired part_XXXXXX_data.parquet and part_XXXXXX_meta.parquet files using effect_family_meta_data_v1. effect_parts.json records class labels, the local class order for each base family, completed file pairs, and counts. Its complete flag is set only after all writes succeed. Readers must use its part list, rather than glob all Parquet files, to exclude stale files from explicitly overwritten runs.

The metadata file stores readname, chrom, strand, the full oriented read sequence, inference_converged, and length once per read. length partitions the flattened data rows in metadata order; it counts selected output positions, not all bases in the sequence. Reads with no selected sites have no output row. The data file stores read_pos, position, family_index, predicted_class_index, isolated_class_index, neighbor_count, canonical_energy, and float32 scores lists. Family indices 0–3 mean A/C/G/T, with -1 for an unrecognized base. For example, a C-centered call stores only [C, 5mC, 5hmC] if those are its fitted classes; it stores no A/G/T/6mA placeholders. An A-centered call may store [A, 6mA]. The actual class order comes from family_class_indices in the manifest, not this example. No-call rows have class indices -1, empty lists, and null canonical energy.

--effect_write_rows 4000000 targets four million rows per part. Flushes occur between complete reads. --effect_write_mb 512 independently bounds the current Arrow buffer and all queued/in-flight writer payloads; compression workspaces and Python/allocator overhead are additional. A read larger than the byte limit fails with a request to raise it. --effect_writer_threads 2 allows concurrent part writers; use 1 when a second writer does not help the storage system. Write failures leave an incomplete manifest. Files use lossless Zstandard level 1 compression, byte-stream splitting for float payloads, and dictionary encoding for low-cardinality integer fields. These storage encodings preserve the float32 values exactly.

docs.title: Read and summarize calls
docs.text:
Use porefm.outputs.open_output for previews, filters, DuckDB queries, and site summaries. Start with the prototype summary recipe and see the shared output API for complete options.

The reader reconstructs class names, k-mers, per-class scores, and call status from the family-local layout. Off-family scores are null. Site summaries exclude negative reference positions, missing chromosomes, and invalid strands. Keep canonical calls in the denominator when calculating modification-call fractions.

For an active run, open_output(path, allow_incomplete=True) takes a snapshot of finished file pairs. Reopen to see later parts. Completed runs use the manifest's exact part list. Do not overwrite a directory while reading it.

The reconstructed isolated_class uses that candidate's full footprint without any other events, not the center-only ablation. canonical_energy is the center's uncorrected whitened residual norm squared and is not a calibrated null p-value. Parquet output contains scores rather than probabilities. Optional BAM output converts the scores as described below. Scores remain uncalibrated. A high canonical energy with poor known-effect fit may indicate an unknown modification or noise; the model does not assign a calibrated unknown class.

Artifacts record the manifest, input paths/metadata, BED hashes, and backbone SHA256; inference also records the fitted artifact hash and run arguments. Use the same backbone for prototype extraction and query inference; checkpoint hash mismatches fail validation. Never load untrusted .pt pickle artifacts.

docs.title: Optional MM/ML BAM output
docs.text:
Add these options to an existing prototype classify --scorer residual-effects command to write both the usual score Parquet files and output.bam under --output_dir:

--output_format both --bam_threads 4 --effect_probability_temperature 1.0

Use --output_format bam for BAM alone; parquet remains the default. The BAM output uses this RNA mapping from Dorado:

Artifact modification label SAM code m5C C+m m6A A+a inosine A+17596 pseU T+17802 2OmeC C+19228 2OmeA A+69426 2OmeG G+19229 2OmeU T+19227

Labels are case-insensitive (Inosine is accepted); 5mC and 6mA are also accepted aliases. The fitted artifact supplies the class order and canonical families. Unknown modification labels, mismatched families, and duplicate codes fail before inference. Only modifications present in the artifact are emitted. RNA uridine groups use T exactly as in the table.

For each callable selected position, probabilities are softmax(family_scores / effect_probability_temperature), including the canonical score in the denominator. Temperature must be finite and positive; the default is 1. It affects only BAM probabilities, not decoding, predicted labels, or Parquet scores. This normalization holds inferred neighbors fixed and is not a calibrated posterior or a marginal over beam paths.

Every modeled modification gets a separate MM group, including low-probability alternatives and sites predicted canonical. Canonical probability is implicit as the remaining mass. Following the SAM tag specification, ML stores min(255, floor(256 * probability)) in group-major order. MN records the full sequence length. Tags use as-sequenced coordinates and + even for reverse alignments. The full source sequence supplies MM delta counts, including clipped bases that were not scored.

The same motif/position selection used by Parquet determines BAM tag sites. Unselected and unavailable-context sites are omitted with the MM ? flag, meaning unknown, not confidently canonical. Each processed read is retained, including reads with no callable selected sites (which receive no MM/ML/MN). Reads rejected by the input filters are not copied to the output.

Sequence, qualities, alignment, and unrelated tags are preserved; input modification tags, raw signal SG, and move-table mv tags are removed, as in supervised BAM output. With explicit sequence polishing, output uses the polished sequence and alignment. Input BAM headers are merged by reference name and RG/PG ID; conflicting definitions fail explicitly. Output is unsorted and unindexed because workers may interleave reads; sort and index it separately if needed for regional tools.

effect_run.json records SAM mappings, temperature, probability semantics, read counts, and BAM completion. The writer publishes output.bam only after successful completion; an interrupted attempt leaves output.bam.partial. The usual output-overwrite safeguards apply. During forced reuse, an older output.bam can remain until the new attempt succeeds, so check this run's completion metadata. Stale indexes are not removed automatically.

docs.title: Prototype scoring and resources
docs.text: For a released bundle and a minimal command, use the prototype guide. This page covers custom artifacts, read-based inputs, and resource tuning.

docs.title: Score a custom model
docs.text:
Use the artifact produced by custom fitting, paired with the exact backbone checkpoint used for that fit. Replace the query paths and contig below with your sample:

backbone=/path/to/backbone-checkpoint

porefm prototype classify \
  --scorer residual-effects --effect_model outputs/prototype_effects/model.pt \
  --bam_path QUERY.signal.bam --ref QUERY.fasta --chrom CONTIG \
  --model_path "$backbone" \
  --size 2048 --step 1800 --num_trim 8 \
  --motif 'N 0' --device cuda --effect_device cuda --disable_compile \
  --effect_beam_width 32 --effect_max_sweeps 8 --effect_threads 4 \
  --output_dir outputs/prototype_effects/query_calls

For an unaligned signal BAM, add --read_based and omit --ref and --chrom:

porefm prototype classify \
  --scorer residual-effects --effect_model outputs/prototype_effects/model.pt \
  --bam_path QUERY.unaligned.signal.bam --read_based \
  --model_path "$backbone" \
  --size 2048 --step 1800 --num_trim 8 \
  --motif 'N 0' --device cuda --effect_device cuda --disable_compile \
  --output_dir outputs/prototype_effects/unaligned_calls

This streams unindexed BAM records, including unmapped reads. Raw signal is required through SG tags or --pod5. Move tables are preferred; supported chemistries can infer chunks when moves are absent. Sequence type, pore chemistry, and k-mer currents come from the matched backbone's metadata. All read chunks supply neighbor evidence; --motif only selects output positions in the called sequence. Missing alignment does not invalidate a read's embeddings. The usual context-support checks and edge trimming still apply. Reference-based --pos_file and polishing options are incompatible.

Output uses zero-based oriented read_pos with position=-1; unmapped reads also have chrom='*' and strand=-1. Mapped records streamed in this mode without --ref retain chromosome/strand metadata but also use position=-1. Identify calls lacking reference coordinates by (readname, read_pos).

Read-based motifs also support optional --ref and --chrom, independently:

--read_based --motif 'A 0;C 0' --ref reference.fa --chrom chr1 chr2

This selects A/C positions in the called read sequence, fetches only reads mapped to chr1/chr2 from sorted, indexed BAMs, and retains their zero-based genomic coordinates on both strands. Insertions and soft clips remain read targets with position=-1 and position=-2, respectively. Without --chrom, all records are streamed, including unmapped reads, even when --ref is supplied. Without --ref, --chrom still filters input but genomic positions remain -1. All chunks of each accepted read continue to supply neighbor evidence.

Do not pass --prototype_embeddings, --class_labels, --class_priors, or --classifier_output: these come from the already fitted artifact. Use --effect_neighbors off for a center-only ablation with the same fitted center effects and noise metric. --effect_penalty explicitly overrides the event cost. Fresh output paths are required; existing files are not overwritten.

docs.title: Devices and resource settings
docs.text:
Classification defaults to --device cuda --effect_device cuda. The first option selects backbone execution; the second selects downstream effect scoring. --device cpu --effect_device cpu requests CPU execution where supported by model dependencies. auto opts into automatic device selection. See installation for the supported GPU setup.

Option Default What it controls --batch_size See command help Backbone chunks per forward pass; reduce for GPU memory pressure. --effect_batch_reads 16 Maximum complete reads grouped for effect preparation. --effect_batch_bases 65536 Base budget for a preparation group; a longer read is handled alone. --effect_block_size 4096 Scoring tile size; smaller tiles reduce working memory. --effect_cache_mb 256 MiB retained for reusable effect tensors; 0 disables the cache. --effect_queue_size 8 Maximum outstanding reads sent to CPU decoding. --effect_queue_mb 256 MiB of accounted queued scores and metadata, including the active read. --effect_decoder auto Numba when available and enabled; python selects the reference decoder.

The fitted model, canonical/noise tables, current tensors, Python overhead, and output buffers use memory in addition to these budgets. A read exceeding the queue byte limit fails with a request to raise it. Decoder traceback storage scales with read length times effective beam width. Tiles do not split a read into independent decoding problems or change the footprint radius.

Numba is installed with PoreFM. Its first use can take longer while kernels compile. --effect_decoder numba requires it to be available with JIT enabled; compilation/runtime errors are reported. The selected decoder is recorded in effect_run.json as decoder_backend.

GPU effect scoring uses float32. CPU/GPU reduction order can produce small rounding differences and change near-tied calls. For controlled comparisons, keep the model, penalty, neighbors, search settings, batching, and software fixed.

Output-buffer controls are described in prototype output files.

docs.title: Supervised labels and training inputs
docs.text: Use these JSON definitions to supply training labels or select inference targets. Training requires SG-tagged signal BAMs. For direct BAM + POD5 inference, see inference inputs.

docs.title: Supervised and inference BAM JSON
docs.text:
JSON files cannot contain comments or trailing commas. Use double quotes for all keys and string values. A training config must define exactly one non-empty sample list:

{
  "config_type": "supervised",
  "schema_version": 1,
  "labelled_samples": [
    {
      "bam_path": "/path/to/modified.bam",
      "ref": "/path/to/reference.fa",
      "contigs": ["chr1", "chr2"],
      "motif": "CG 0;CH 0",
      "motif_label": "1;2"
    }
  ]
}

bam_path may name one BAM or a directory, which is recursively expanded to naturally sorted *.bam files. Keep a directory free of both merged BAMs and their component shards, or reads will be duplicated.

docs.title: Labelled sample modes
docs.text:
Mode Required fields Forbidden or ignored fields Read-based motif bam_path, read_based: true, motif, motif_label pos_file is forbidden; ref is unused for training labels; inference can retain reference coordinates Reference motif bam_path, ref, motif, motif_label Omit read_based or set it to false Explicit positions bam_path, ref, pos_file read_based: true is forbidden

Common labelled-sample fields:

  • contigs: JSON array of contig strings. Omit or use [] for all reference contigs. For SG input, supplying contigs in read-based mode selects indexed regional fetching. Direct POD5 inference uses its read-ID index instead.
  • motif: one string containing semicolon-delimited motif specifications. Each specification is IUPAC_PATTERN ZERO_BASED_OFFSET; the offset selects the base inside the motif and is not a class index.
  • motif_label: class indices separated with semicolons. Every index must be in [0, num_classes) and order must match motif; if fewer labels than motifs are supplied, the final label applies to the remaining motifs.
  • sample_labels: probability of retaining each label occurrence; default 1.
  • label_smoothing: optional classification epsilon overriding the config/CLI default; explicit 0 disables smoothing for this sample.
  • flag: additional SAM flag bits to exclude; default 0.
  • polish: boolean, default false. Polishing requires mapped records with CIGAR and MD information.
  • polish_indel_limit: largest corrected unmasked indel; default 5.
  • polish_vcf_path: optional VCF/BCF whose ALT SNPs and indel loci are preserved. Prefer indexed input for large files.

Set the class count with --num_classes, not in the sample JSON.

docs.title: Reference-position files
docs.text:
Position files referenced by pos_file are tab-separated, have no header, use zero-based reference coordinates, and contain:

chromosome<TAB>position<TAB>strand<TAB>class_0<TAB>...<TAB>class_K-1

Strand may be +, -, 0, or 1; provide exactly one numeric target column per classifier class.

docs.title: Tagged sample mode
docs.text:
Use tagged_samples instead of labelled_samples:

{
  "config_type": "supervised",
  "schema_version": 1,
  "tagged_samples": [
    {
      "bam_path": "/path/to/tagged.bam",
      "read_label_dict_path": "/path/to/read_labels.pkl",
      "label_coordinates": "read",
      "label_smoothing": 0
    }
  ]
}

Every dictionary-labelled tagged sample must explicitly set label_coordinates to "read" or "ref"; there is no default. Both systems are zero-based:

  • "read" uses the original 5'-to-3' read sequence, including soft clips and insertions. Reverse alignments use offsets in get_forward_sequence(), not the stored reverse-complemented BAM sequence. No FASTA is consulted. Omit contigs to stream mapped or unmapped records without an index; explicit contigs still require indexed regional fetching.
  • "ref" uses positions on the read's reference contig, including on reverse alignments, and requires mapped/indexed BAM plus matching indexed FASTA supplied as ref.

Choose one label source:

  • Set ML_tag: true to decode MM/ML calls; it defaults to false. Calls with probability strictly greater than ML_threshold (default 0.5) receive label. Optional negative_label assigns calls strictly below the same threshold a different class; omission or null leaves those calls ignored. Calls exactly at the threshold are always ignored. The fraction of decoded calls retained across both enabled classes must meet min_read_frac (default 0); its denominator is decoded calls, not all read bases. This path still requires a mapped, indexed BAM and ref; omit the dictionary-only label_coordinates field.
  • Set optional MM_code to one exact SAM modification code, such as "a" or numeric 17596 (also accepted as "17596"). It selects calls before thresholding: label, negative_label, and the min_read_frac denominator all apply only to that code. Reads without selected calls are skipped. Use the code actually present in MM, not a class name such as "m6A" or a full group header such as "A+a". Letter/numeric aliases are not inferred. This option requires ML_tag: true.
  • Otherwise provide read_label_dict_path, a pickle keyed by read name. Reads absent from the dictionary are skipped. The path has no default when ML_tag is false and is mutually exclusive with ML_tag: true.
  • label defaults to class index 1. negative_label is only supported with ML_tag: true and must be a valid class index different from label. label_smoothing, flag, and polishing fields use the labelled-sample defaults above.

For class order A 6mA, this sample uses both sides of the threshold:

{
  "tagged_samples": [{
    "bam_path": "/path/to/data/signal.sorted.bam",
    "ref": "/path/to/references/genome.fa",
    "ML_tag": true,
    "MM_code": "a",
    "ML_threshold": 0.5,
    "label": 1,
    "negative_label": 0
  }]
}

The loader constructs one-hot targets, not ML probability vectors. The supervised loss applies the resolved label_smoothing afterward. Only explicitly decoded calls are eligible; unlisted bases are not inferred to be negative. With MM_code, interleaved codes are decoded separately and selected positions are sorted in original read orientation. Duplicate selected positions raise an error rather than assigning ambiguous targets. Omitting MM_code pools calls across codes and requires sorted coordinates. One sample with MM_code selects at most one code and maps it to one positive class; this is not a multi-code-to-multiclass mapping.

Dictionary entries have the form read_name: (target_values, target_positions). Use (N, num_classes) probability arrays for per-position vectors; a shared (num_classes,) vector or scalar class is also accepted. Position arrays must contain sorted, unique, nonnegative integers; sort target rows together with positions. For three-class C/5mC/5hmC targets, columns must follow exactly that model class order. A one-dimensional array of length num_classes is interpreted as a shared probability vector, so use explicit two-dimensional one-hot arrays for per-site hard labels.

For dictionary labels, output position follows the selected coordinate system. When polishing is enabled, original read targets are remapped into polished coordinates and targets on removed insertions are dropped. Polishing still requires aligned reads. Read and reference dictionaries produce the same labels when they describe the same aligned bases; insertion/soft-clip targets have no reference equivalent, and a deleted reference base has no original read coordinate.

docs.title: Classifier modification metadata
docs.text:
Supply --base and --mod_code to porefm finetune-modification to save the canonical base and modification codes in checkpoint meta.base and meta.mod_code. For example, use --num_classes 3 --class_labels C 5mC 5hmC --base C --mod_code m h. Class 0 is canonical; provide exactly one code for each remaining class, in logit order. Codes are stored as strings, including numeric codes. These options are optional for training.

With --model_load_path, omitted values inherit from the classifier checkpoint. When extending its class count, supply the complete updated code list. porefm detect-modification automatically uses the saved values. Explicit --base and --mod_code override their respective metadata fields. BAM output (--output_format bam or both) requires modification codes from metadata or the CLI; Parquet output does not.

docs.title: Classification label smoothing
docs.text:
Supervised fine-tuning resolves label_smoothing for each sample using sample > config > --label_smoothing > 0. Values must be finite numbers in [0, 1); omission inherits the next level, while explicit zero overrides it. Every BAM expanded from a sample directory inherits that sample's value.

For example, native labels can inherit a config default while reliable IVT or PCR controls opt out (paths below are illustrative):

{
  "label_smoothing": 0.02,
  "labelled_samples": [
    {
      "bam_path": "/path/to/data/native.bam",
      "ref": "/path/to/references/genome.fa",
      "pos_file": "/path/to/labels/native.tsv"
    },
    {
      "bam_path": "/path/to/data/ivt.bam",
      "read_based": true,
      "motif": "A 0",
      "motif_label": 0,
      "label_smoothing": 0
    }
  ]
}

For target distribution q, class count C, and resolved epsilon e, the loss uses (1 - e) * q + e / C. This applies once in float32 to retained classification bases with either cross-entropy or focal loss. It works for motifs, position files, per-read dictionaries, and MM/ML labels. Metrics use the original targets. Zero preserves supplied soft target distributions; it does not convert them to hard labels. The setting is training metadata and does not alter classifier inference.

Startup logs list each sample's effective value and whether it came from the sample, config, or CLI. On continuation, the supplied configs/CLI determine the run's smoothing policy. Exclusion samples always use zero. Knowing that one class is absent in a multiclass sample remains an exclusion constraint, not a hard label choosing among the other classes.

docs.title: Top-level supervision
docs.text:
Omitting supervision means ordinary classification. To select it explicitly, use "supervision": {"type": "classification"}; include it alongside a complete labelled_samples or tagged_samples list.

Classification supervision accepts no fields other than type. The optional label_smoothing setting belongs alongside supervision at the JSON top level or inside a sample, not inside the supervision object.

Exclusion supervision applies to the entire JSON file and currently supports only labelled_samples:

{
  "config_type": "supervised",
  "schema_version": 1,
  "supervision": {
    "type": "exclusion",
    "excluded_class": "5mC",
    "expected_allowed_proportions": {"C": 0.8, "5hmC": 0.2},
    "proportion_tolerance": 0.05
  },
  "labelled_samples": [
    {
      "bam_path": "/path/to/no_5mc.bam",
      "ref": "/path/to/reference.fa",
      "motif": "CG 0",
      "motif_label": "1"
    }
  ]
}

Strict exclusion requirements:

  • excluded_class must exactly match one unique --class_labels value.
  • JSON label_smoothing must be zero or omitted at both config and sample levels. Exclusion loss always ignores the CLI smoothing fallback.
  • Every motif label must equal the excluded class index.
  • If expected proportions are present, they must name every allowed class exactly once, contain finite nonnegative values summing to one, and be paired with proportion_tolerance in [0, 1).
  • Put biologically different exclusions or expected mixtures in separate JSON files. Each file becomes one supervision and sampling group.
  • Supply one --group_weights value per --bam_config file. These are source selection weights, not class weights.
